newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Discouraged Australian jobless give up work search.
newsitem.headline: Discouraged Australian jobless give up work search.

text.p: Australian unemployment fell to its lowest level so far this year in June but economists said the apparent good news disguised a weak labour market that pointed to yet another interest rate cut.

Official figures released on Thursday showed unemployment dropped to 8.5 percent in June, its lowest level since last November, from 8.8 percent in May, as total employment rose by 11,900 in the month.

But the employment rise was well below forecasts of a 42,500 rise, which would have reversed a 40,300 fall in May, and analysts said unemployment only fell because many people had given up the search for work.
"Continued falls in the participation rate suggest that strong disincentive effects are at work, and that people have just given up looking for jobs," Societe Generale economist Glenn Maguire said.
The Australian dollar slipped and and bond futures firmed on a feeling that the weak data would put pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to cut official interest rates again.
The RBA has cut the official cash rate four times in the past year, each time by half a percentage point. The last cut, on May 23, took it down to 5.5 percent.
But the rate cuts have yet to create a feel-good effect flowing through fully to consumer and business confidence.
Thursday's data showed that while the number of unemployed people fell by 32,000 in June, this was mainly due to a fall of 20,400 people who were looking for work.

The inability of the economy to generate jobs growth had so discouraged job seekers that they had left the workforce -- the participation rate fell to a three year low of 63.0 percent in June, down from 63.2 percent in May and 63.5 percent in April.
The participation rate measures the labour force -- employed people and unemployed people looking for work -- as a percentage of the working-age population.
While the working age population has increased by 34,400 in the past two months, the labour force has fallen by 52,900.
"Had the participation rate been at the April level of 63.5 percent, the June unemployment rate would have been over nine percent," Westpac senior economist John Peters said.
For its part, the government focused on the lower unemployment rate, and described the jobs outlook as positive.
"I would take today's figures, showing a fall in unemployment from 8.8 (percent) to 8.5 (percent), as a very good sign," Treasurer Peter Costello said.
But while the fall in people looking for work had led to an improvement in the unemployment rate, economists said it could not hide the underlying weakness of the jobs market.

Total employment has fallen by 4,000 in the first six months of 1997, and within that full-time employment has been especially weak, falling by 40,000 in the last two months and by 63,900 over the first six months of the year.

Given that the stalled labour market has been a factor in the four rate cuts seen since last July, Thursday's data saw market speculation of a near term rate cut by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) intensify.

A cut could happen as soon as Friday but most felt that any move would not occur until after the release of June quarter inflation and wages data in two weeks, or until after the RBA's August 5 board meeting.
